extName.message: Enhancer for Plane — Quick Open & Issue Templates
extName.description: Extension name shown in the Chrome Web Store and browser.

extShort.description: The brand on its own — the name you can say out loud. Used where a name has to be short: the popup and settings headers, and the toolbar tooltip. extName adds the searchable half after it.

extDesc.message: Issue templates, quick open by key, copy reference, and a focus mode that hides the side panels — inside the Plane UI.
extDesc.description: Short description shown in the Chrome Web Store, and the extension's own description in chrome://extensions. Features and where they appear, nothing else: an extension not touching the server is not news, "the open-source Jira alternative" only spent characters on a reader already looking at a Plane extension, and the searchable spellings (makeplane, plane.so) sit at the foot of the store description.

cmdToggleFocus.message: Focus mode: hide or show the side panels
cmdToggleFocus.description: Shown in chrome://extensions/shortcuts, where the user can rebind the key. It has to say what the shortcut does with no surrounding UI to lean on.

optTagline.message: Fills the gaps in Plane — quick open, issue templates, copy reference, focus mode, width rules. Quick open works on Jira and Linear too.
optTagline.description: Sub-line under the settings header. It names features and nothing else — whoever is reading it installed the extension, so neither what Plane is nor how it is spelled on GitHub belongs here. Order matches extName: quick open first. Two lines is the budget, and the harness measures it in both locales.

optFeedback.description: Header link to the GitHub issue tracker. Deliberately an invitation, not "Report an issue" — most of what arrives is an idea or a question, and the narrower wording turned the tracker into a place you only visit when something is broken.

optDomainsDesc.message: Runs only on the domains listed below. One per line. Wildcards like *.example.com are supported. Saving prompts Chrome to grant access to each newly added domain.

optDomainsAll.message: Run on all sites (ignore the list below)

optDomainsTip.message: Tip: to enable the current tab's Plane instance, open the toolbar popup and click “Enable on this site.”

optFocusDesc.message: A rule marked “Only while focus mode is on” stays out of the way until you ask for it. Two ship ready to use: hide a work item's properties panel, and hide the left navigation. A third caps the reading width and starts switched off.

optFocusHow.message: Three ways in: Alt+Shift+F (macOS ⌥+⇧+F), the toggle beside a work item's key, and the switch in the toolbar popup. To rebind the shortcut, open chrome://extensions/shortcuts.

optFocusScope.message: It applies to the tab you turned it on in, survives a reload there, and is gone once you close that tab. It never syncs to your other devices.

optRulesTitle.description: Was "Style rules (width / length)" while every shipped rule set a width. Focus mode's presets set display and padding in the same list, so the parenthetical had become a promise the card no longer keeps; the description under it says what a rule is instead.

optRulesDesc.message: Force a property : value onto any CSS selector (with !important). If Plane's class names change, just edit the selector. Type the full value with units, e.g. 320px, 30rem, 55ch.

optRulesEmpty.message: No rules yet. Click “Add rule” to start.

optPresetFocusProps.message: Focus: hide the work item properties panel

optPresetFocusWidth.message: Focus: centre the body at a reading width
optPresetFocusWidth.description: Ships switched off — capping the line length is a preference, unlike hiding a panel the user just asked to hide.

optRuleFocusOnly.message: Only while focus mode is on

optTplDesc1.message: Pick one from the “Template” button next to “Attach” in an item's description toolbar — it fills the title and the body together. The title is optional.

optTplDesc2.message: The body is written in Markdown and rendered into the editor: ## headings, - / 1. lists, - [ ] checkboxes, **bold**, `code`.

optTplDesc3.message: Variables (filled on insert): {{date}} today, {{date+N}}/{{date-N}} N days from today (e.g. {{date+7}}), {{week}} this week's range (Mon–Sun), {{month}} as YYYY-MM. Shortcut: Alt/⌥+T opens templates while editing a description.

optTplEmpty.message: No templates yet. Click “Add template” to start.

optTplShareDesc.message: Share with your team saves your own templates as a file your teammates can subscribe to. Host it where they can reach it over https and give them the URL — they add it under Template sync below. Templates you received from a source are not included.

optTplTitlePh.message: Title (e.g. [Bug] — leave empty to skip the title)

optVarsDesc.message: Values you can drop into any template — your own and synced ones alike — as {{var.name}}. A synced template can say {{var.team}} and resolve to a different value for each person who inserts it.

optVarsUndefined.message: The var. prefix keeps your names from ever clashing with the built-in {{date}}, {{week}} and {{month}}. A variable you have not defined stays visible as {{var.name}} rather than turning into an empty string.

optVarsEmpty.message: No variables yet. Click “Add variable” to start.

msgVarBadName.message: Use letters, numbers, hyphen or underscore only.

msgVarDupe.message: Another variable already uses this name.

msgVarLimit.message: Up to $MAX$ variables. Remove one to add another.

msgSrcLimit.message: Up to $MAX$ sync sources. Remove one to add another.

optSyncDesc.message: Pull shared templates from one or more URLs, checked on browser start, on a schedule, and when you open this page. Synced templates are read-only — edit them at the source. Host the file on the same domain as Plane to avoid a separate access prompt.

optSyncFormatDesc.message: A flat list; each item carries its own group string. The top-level name labels the whole collection and is used when you leave a source's name blank.

optSrcUrlPh.description: Placeholder text: an example URL. Nothing here is prose.

optBackupDesc1.message: Export all settings (domains, style rules, templates, variables, sync source URLs, and quick open links) to a JSON file, or import a previously exported file. Imported settings load into the form — review, then Save to apply.

optBackupDesc2.message: The file lists your domains, source URLs and variable values in plain text — so if a variable holds your name, or those addresses are private, treat the file as internal. Synced templates are not included: they re-download from their source after you Save.

optStorageNote.message: Settings sync across your devices via Chrome, which allows ~100 KB in total. Templates are stored in blocks of ~8 KB, so any one template has to fit a single block.

msgInvalidSrcUrl.message: A source URL must start with http:// or https://

msgSrcEnterUrl.message: Enter a URL, then Save to sync.

msgSrcNotSynced.message: Not synced yet — Save, then “Sync now”.

msgSrcSkipped.description: Appended to msgSrcSynced, so the leading space is deliberate — without it the two run together as "12 templates(3 skipped".

msgSrcLastGood.description: Appended to msgSrcFailed. Leading space deliberate, as with msgSrcSkipped.

msgSrcHidden.description: Appended to a source's summary line. Leading space deliberate.

msgChangedElsewhere.message: Settings changed elsewhere (e.g. the picker). Reload this page to apply them — unsaved edits will be lost.

msgLoadedPicked.message: Loaded the rule added by the picker.

msgFeedNamePrompt.message: Name this set of templates. A teammate sees it as the source's name unless they rename it. Leave empty to skip.

msgFeedEmpty.message: Nothing to share yet — add a template of your own first. Templates you received from a source are not included.

msgFeedExported.message: Saved $COUNT$ templates to a file. Host it over https, then share the URL.

msgFeedExportedCapped.message: Saved $COUNT$ templates — the most a synced source can hold — so $DROPPED$ were left out. Host the file over https and share the URL.

msgImported.message: Imported — review, then click Save to apply.

msgImportInvalid.message: Import failed: not a valid settings JSON.

msgImportNotOurs.message: Import failed: that file was not exported by this extension.

msgImportIsSyncFile.message: That looks like a template sync file, not a settings backup. Add its URL under Template sync instead.

msgImportNewer.message: Import failed: that backup is from a newer version (schema $FILE$, this build reads $HERE$). Update the extension first.

msgImportUnreadable.message: Import failed: could not read file.

msgSaveFirst.message: Save first — “Sync now” fetches the saved sources.

msgResetConfirm.message: Reset all settings to defaults. Continue?

msgSavedNoPerm.message: Saved — but site access was denied, so listed domains stay inactive until you grant it.

msgSaveQuota.message: Save failed: settings exceed the ~$LIMIT$ KB Chrome sync allows in total. Shorten or remove templates (or keep a JSON backup).

msgSaveQuotaItem.message: Save failed: your domains and style rules together exceed the ~$LIMIT$ KB Chrome sync allows for one block. Remove some, or keep a JSON backup.

msgSaveTplTooLarge.message: Save failed: the template “$NAME$” is on its own larger than the ~$LIMIT$ KB Chrome sync allows for one block. Shorten it, or keep it in a JSON backup instead.

msgStorageOver.message: — over the sync limit; saving may fail
msgStorageOver.description: Appended to msgStorageUsed. Leading space deliberate.

msgStorageOverItem.message: — one block is over its ~$LIMIT$ KB limit; saving will fail
msgStorageOverItem.description: Appended to msgStorageUsed. Leading space deliberate.

msgStorageNear.description: Appended to msgStorageUsed. Leading space deliberate.

popNotLoaded.message: Not loaded here — reload the page (Ctrl/Cmd+R).

popNotLoadedShort.message: Not loaded here — reload the page.

popRescanOpen.message: Re-scanned. Open a work item's description.

pickHeader.message: Create a rule from a selector  ·  Esc to cancel

pickerHint.message: Click an element to create a rule · Esc to cancel

pickNoSelector.message: Couldn't build a selector for that element.

pickRuleAdded.message: Rule added: $SELECTOR$ — open Settings to set the value.

pickRuleFailed.message: Failed to save the rule (storage error).

optCopyDesc.message: On a work item — its own page, or the panel a list opens — the button beside its ID (or <kbd>Alt</kbd>/<kbd>⌥</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd>) copies that item to your clipboard in one of the formats below. Use it to hand a work item to a chat message, a pull request, or a branch name.

optCopyTokens.message: Three values can be filled in: {{item.key}}, {{item.title}} and {{item.url}}. Everything else in a format is copied exactly as you typed it, so the preview under each row is what lands on the clipboard.

optCopyEmpty.message: No formats yet. Click “Add format” to start.

optCopyFormatPh.description: Placeholder text, and an example of the format language. {{item.key}} and {{item.title}} are tokens the expander looks for — translate around them, never inside them.

focusBtnTitle.message: Turn focus mode on: hide the side panels  ·  Alt+Shift+F (⌥+⇧+F)
focusBtnTitle.description: Title and aria-label of the toggle beside a work item's key. The two states are a matching pair naming the action, not a label and a status line — the pressed state is what says which position it is in. Both name the shortcut, because the button is also where people find out it exists.

focusBtnOnTitle.message: Turn focus mode off: show the side panels  ·  Alt+Shift+F (⌥+⇧+F)

msgCopiedMissing.message: Copied, but $FIELDS$ could not be read — it stayed in the text as written.

msgCopyFailed.message: Could not reach the clipboard. Copy it by hand from the preview in Settings.

msgCopyNoItem.message: No work item on this page — open one, or click a row to open its panel.

msgFocusOn.message: Focus mode on — Alt+Shift+F (⌥+⇧+F) brings the panels back.

msgFocusRestored.message: Focus mode is still on in this tab — Alt+Shift+F (⌥+⇧+F) brings the panels back.
msgFocusRestored.description: Shown once per page load, not on the toggle. A reload is the one way to meet a hidden properties panel without having just asked for it.

msgCopyLimit.message: Up to $MAX$ formats. Remove one to add another.

msgCopyUnknownToken.message: Not a value that can be filled in: $FIELDS$. It is copied as written.

msgExampleAdded.message: Added our example feed. Press Save to fetch it — Chrome will ask for access to raw.githubusercontent.com once.

msgExampleExists.message: Our example feed is already in your sources.

optPermTitle.message: This device needs to approve access

optPermDesc.message: Your settings synced here, but Chrome keeps site access per device — so $COUNT$ of the sites and sources you listed are not approved on this one yet. Until you approve them, the extension stays inactive here.

badgeNeedsAccess.message: Enhancer for Plane — approve access on this device

popPermGap.message: ⚠ Some sites need access on this device — open Settings to approve.

optKeysDesc.message: Everything the keyboard reaches, in one place. On macOS, <kbd>Alt</kbd> is <kbd>⌥</kbd> Option.

optKeysTplWhere.message: While editing a description, and in the “Create work item” dialog

optKeysCopyWhere.message: On a work item — its own page, or the panel a list opens. Not while you are typing.

optKeysFocus.message: Turn focus mode on or off

optKeysFocusWhere.message: Anywhere the extension runs, including while you are typing

optKeysJump.message: Open a work item by key

optKeysJumpWhere.message: The address bar, on any tab

optKeysThenKey.description: Follows the literal omnibox keyword: “issue” then the key. Not a modifier combination, which is why it reads as words.

optKeysRebind.message: Focus mode is a browser command, so you can rebind it — or clear it — at chrome://extensions/shortcuts. The other two are handled inside the page and are fixed.

optKeysWhyTyping.message: <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>T</kbd> is meant to be used mid-sentence, so it works while you type. <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd> deliberately does not: on macOS <kbd>⌥</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd> is the character “ç”, and a shortcut that swallows it out of a title would take more than it gives.

optKeysWhyCommand.message: Focus mode escapes that trade-off by being a browser command rather than a key handler in the page — Chrome intercepts it before the page ever sees the key.

optQuickDesc.message: In the address bar type issue, a space, then a work item key such as PROJ-123 — Enter opens it. The key’s prefix picks the target, so you can point ENG- at Linear and leave the rest on Plane; a target with an empty prefix is the default. It is on the toolbar popup too.

optQuickTokens.message: Put {{key}} where the key belongs in the URL — {{key.proj}} and {{key.num}} are its two halves. A URL with no {{key}} gets the key appended to the end. The line under each row shows where a sample key would land.

optQuickEmpty.message: No quick links yet. Click “Add quick link”.

optQuickUrlPh.description: Placeholder text. {{key}} is a token the expander looks for; the ellipsis stands in for a host. Do not translate either.

optQuickPreview.description: Layout only — a key, an arrow, the URL it lands on. No words to translate.

omniboxHint.message: Type a work item key to open it

omniboxNoTarget.message: No quick link set — Enter opens Settings
